name: claude-quenching
description: Marketplace hosting the claude-quenching plugin: a three-front aligner (docs/ OKF bundle, native specs/ spec-driven workspace, .claude/ skill surface) with one conductor over all three, plus an inserter, task-backlog capturer and triager, knowledge-capturer, glossary-curator, memory-to-docs migrator, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md harness-refactorer, external-source importer, skill minter, run-to-convergence cycle, and a native plan cycle (no external CLI, no delta) for the Claude Code surface of any repository.

plugins.name: claude-quenching
plugins.description: Forces any repository's three quenching fronts into one canonical shape and keeps them conformant: the docs/ Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.1) bundle, the native specs/ spec-driven workspace, and the .claude/ skill + command surface. One symmetric interface across all three — every front has an align (structure, one pass) and an align-and-update (structure plus content, looped to a fixpoint) — plus /align and /align-and-update, which run all three in dependency order on one confirmation. Twenty-seven skills, all under one quenching-<front>-<object>-<verb> taxonomy: the four conductors, the three aligns, docs-add (any doc), docs-learn (concepts), docs-define + docs-glossary-backfill (the fixed A–Z term lookup), docs-import-memory (drain project memory), docs-harness (thin CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md pointers), skill-new (mint a skill), docs-import (external sources), docs-documentation-build (the mkdocs site over the documentation/ home), and the specs-* family driving the native plan cycle — explore, propose, apply, update, archive (with an OKF distillation bridge into docs/), abandon (a plan that will not be built), from-claude (turn a Claude Code plan into an archivable one), the backlog-add/-triage task inbox, the read-only status, and the align/align-and-update pair. Entirely native: no external CLI, no delta, no separate spec store — a plan writes durable rules straight into docs/standards/, and two stdlib Python tools (okf-validate.py, specs.py) enforce and drive it. Every skill is user-invocable: false behind a thin command wrapper (/docs:*, /specs:*, /skill:*, and the root /align, /align-and-update). Every repository that adopts it looks the same.
